What's the difference between a cocoon and a chrysalis?

Butterflies form a hard chrysalis with no silk, while moths spin a silk cocoon around themselves.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakaiba ng cocoon at chrysalis?

Gumagawa ang mariposa ng matigas na chrysalis na walang sutla, samantalang ang moth ay nagtatayo ng cocoon mula sa sutla.
copy.bis:
Unsay kalainan sa cocoon ug chrysalis?

Ang mariposa maghimo og gahi nga chrysalis nga walay sutla, samtang ang moth maghimo og silk cocoon sa palibot sa iyang kaugalingon.

Where does silk fabric come from?

From a moth! The domestic silkworm's larvae feed on mulberry leaves and spin the silk that's used to make fabric.
copy.tl:
Saan galing ang sutlang ginagamit sa tela?

Mula sa isang moth! Ang larva ng domestic silkworm ay kumakain ng dahon ng mulberry at gumagawa ng sutlang ginagamit sa tela.
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang sutla nga gigamit sa tela?

Gikan sa moth! Ang larva sa domestic silkworm nagkaon sa dahon sa mulberry ug naghimo og sutla nga gigamit sa tela.

Why is quiet Mount Pinatubo still being watched?

Pinatubo's magma chamber hasn't fully hardened since 1991! PHIVOLCS keeps seismographs and tiltmeters around it to spot any early changes and keep everyone safe.

Bakit ang tahimik na Mount Pinatubo ay binabantayan pa rin?

Hindi pa tuluyang tumatagas ang magma chamber ng Pinatubo mula 1991! May mga seismograph at tiltmeter ang PHIVOLCS sa paligid nito para makita ang anumang pagbabago at maprotektahan ang lahat.
copy.bis:
Nganong gipangbantayan gihapon ang hilumon nga Mount Pinatubo?

Wala pa hingpit nga magtigas ang magma chamber sa Pinatubo sukad 1991! Adunay mga seismograph ug tiltmeter ang PHIVOLCS sa palibot niini aron makit-an ang bisan unsang pagbag-o ug maprotektahan ang tanan.

Why are mountaintops so cold?

The top of a tall mountain is colder than its base because the air gets colder the higher you go up!
copy.tl:
Bakit malalamig ang mga tuktok ng bundok?

Mas malamig ang tuktok ng mataas na bundok kaysa sa paanan nito dahil bumababa ang temperatura habang tumataas ka!
copy.bis:
Ngano nga bugnaw ang mga tumoy sa bukid?

Mas bugnaw ang tumoy sa taas nga bukid kaysa sa tiilan niini tungod kay mosaka ka, mobugnaw ang hangin!

copy.en: Even in hot tropical countries, very tall mountains can have snow on top all year! At that height, it's freezing cold — even when it's hot at the base.
copy.tl: Kahit sa mainit na tropikal na bansa, ang napakatataas na bundok ay maaaring may niyebe sa tuktok buong taon! Sa ganoong taas, sobrang lamig — kahit mainit sa paanan.
copy.bis: Bisan sa init nga tropikal nga nasud, ang taas kaayo nga bukid mahimong adunay niyebe sa tumoy tibuok tuig! Sa maong gitas-on, bugnaw kaayo — bisan init sa tiilan.

Can mountains disappear over time?

Yes! Over very long times, water, ice, and wind slowly wear mountains down until the land becomes much flatter.
copy.tl:
Mawawala ba ang mga bundok sa pagtagal?

Oo! Sa napakahabang panahon, unti-unting pinapababa ng tubig, yelo, at hangin ang mga bundok hanggang maging mas pantay ang lupa.
copy.bis:
Mawala ba ang mga bukid sa paglabay sa panahon?

Oo! Sa hataas kaayo nga panahon, ang tubig, yelo, ug hangin hinay-hinay nga magpaubos sa mga bukid hangtod mahimong mas patag ang yuta.

How do some fish protect their eggs?

Some fish, like certain tilapia, keep their eggs safe inside their own mouth until the baby fish hatch out!

Paano iniingatan ng ilang isda ang kanilang itlog?

May mga isda, tulad ng ilang tilapia, na inilalagay ang itlog sa loob ng bibig nila hanggang mapisa ang mga sanggol na isda!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpanalipod sa pipila ka isda ang ilang itlog?

Ang pipila ka isda, sama sa ubang tilapia, magbutang sa itlog sulod sa ilang baba hangtod mapusa ang gagmayng isda!

copy.tl: Ang ilang uri ng mudskipper ay hindi mangangaso — mas gusto nilang kumain ng lumot at maliliit na halaman sa ibabaw ng putik!
copy.bis: Ang ubang matang sa mudskipper dili manukob — mas ganahan sila mokaon og lumot ug gagmay nga tanom sa ibabaw sa lapok!

Why can both cheeks swell with mumps?

There's a saliva gland in each cheek, so both can swell and round out the face — though sometimes only one side puffs up.

Bakit namamaga ang parehong pisngi sa beke?

May glandula ng laway sa bawat pisngi, kaya pwedeng mamaga ang dalawa at bumilog ang mukha — minsan isang gilid lang ang namamaga.
copy.bis:
Nganong mohubag ang duha ka aping sa beke?

Adunay glandula sa laway sa matag aping, mao nga mahimong mohubag ang duha ug molingin ang nawong — usahay usa ra ka kilid ang mohubag.

copy.bis: Ang atong mga unod naggamit sa enerhiya gikan sa pagkaon aron makahimo og trabaho! Kini ang naghatag kanato og kusog sa paglakaw ug pagbayaw.

Which animal headbutts with great force?

The musk ox! It's so strong it can charge and headbutt hard with its horns to protect itself.

Aling hayop ang bumabangga nang sobrang lakas?

Ang musk ox! Napakalakas nito—kaya nitong bumangga at gumamit ng sungay nang sobrang lakas para ipagtanggol ang sarili.
copy.bis:
Unsang mananap ang mobangga nga kusgan kaayo?

Ang musk ox! Kusgan kaayo kini—makabangga ug makagamit sa iyang sungay nga kusog aron manalipod sa kaugalingon.

Who is the pascal named after?

It's named after Blaise Pascal, a French scientist and mathematician who studied pressure!

Kanino ipinangalan ang pascal?

Ipinangalan ito kay Blaise Pascal, isang Pranses na siyentista at matematiko na nag-aral ng presyon!
copy.bis:
Kinsay gipangalanan sa pascal?

Ginganlan kini kang Blaise Pascal, usa ka Pranses nga siyentista ug matematiko nga nagtuon sa presyon!

copy.bis: Ang narra mao ang nasudnong kahoy sa Pilipinas — usa ka dakong kahoy nga adunay lig-on nga kahoy nga gigamit sa muwebles ug mamulak og humot nga dilaw nga bulak!

Are wild pigs the same as farm pigs?

No! Wild native pigs are smaller, hairier, and live in the forest — very different from the farm pigs we raise.

Pareho ba ang ligaw at alagang baboy?

Hindi pala! Mas maliit, mas mabalahibo, at nakatira sa gubat ang katutubong ligaw na baboy — iba ito sa alagang baboy sa bukid.
copy.bis:
Managsama ba ang ihalas ug binuhi nga baboy?

Dili diay! Mas gamay, mas baga og balahibo, ug nagpuyo sa lasang ang lumad nga ihalas nga baboy — lahi kini sa binuhi nga baboy sa uma.

It makes its own light in its tail to find a mate in the dark -- that's why it's out and glowing at night!
copy.tl:
Bakit kumikinang ang alitaptap sa gabi?

Gumagawa ito ng sariling ilaw sa puwit nito para makahanap ng kapareha sa dilim -- kaya ito lumalabas at kumikinang tuwing gabi!
copy.bis:
Ngano mosiga ang aninipot sa gabii?

Mohimo kini og kaugalingong kahayag sa ikog aron makakita og kapares sa kangitngit -- mao nga migawas ug mosiga kini sa gabii!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil, sand, and stones do not dissolve in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card only notes that some materials do not dissolve in water. It does not describe uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, suspensions, or their everyday usefulness, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil, sand, and stones do not dissolve in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions dissolving but never identifies a solute, solvent, or solution, nor explains their roles. It provides no direct instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
Does everything dissolve in water?

Nope! Oil, sand, and stones do not dissolve in water; they just stay separate.
copy.tl:
Natutunaw ba ang lahat sa tubig?

Hindi! Ang langis, buhangin, at bato ay hindi natutunaw sa tubig; nananatili silang hiwalay.
copy.bis:
Matunaw ba ang tanan sa tubig?

Dili! Ang lana, balas, ug bato dili matunaw sa tubig; magpabilin silang bulag.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The hot steam spins a turbine to make electricity.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how high voltage electricity from power plants is generated and safely distributed to industries, businesses, and homes, including the role of substations (grid stations), and electric meters
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes only the basic generation step (steam turbine) of a nuclear plant. The competency requires describing how high voltage electricity is generated and safely distributed, including substations and electric meters. The card does not address high voltage, distribution, or safety, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A nuclear plant uses fission heat to boil water!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions heat boiling water, which is a change of state (liquid to gas), but it does not explain the role of heat energy in change of state processes. It simply states that fission heat boils water without explaining the process or the role of heat energy. Thus it is only related to the topic.

copy.en: A nuclear plant uses fission heat to boil water! The hot steam spins a turbine to make electricity.
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang nuclear plant ng init ng fission para magpakulo ng tubig! Ang singaw ang umiikot sa turbine para makagawa ng kuryente.
copy.bis: Ang nuclear plant naggamit sa init sa fission aron pabukalon ang tubig! Ang singaw maoy nagtuyok sa turbine aron makahimo og kuryente.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: there are exactly eight planets zooming around in our amazing Solar System
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the general structure of the solar system, identifying the names of the major celestial objects, their main features, and general composition
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the number of planets in the solar system. It does not describe the general structure, name the major celestial objects, or give their main features or composition, so it does not directly support the competency's required content.

copy.en: Did you know there are exactly eight planets zooming around in our amazing Solar System?
copy.tl: Alam mo ba na may eksaktong walong planeta na umiikot sa ating kamangha-manghang Solar System?
copy.bis: Nahibalo ba ka nga adunay eksakto nga walo ka planeta nga naglibot sa atong kamatingalahon nga Solar System?

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In incomplete metamorphosis, the nymph already looks like the adult insect, just smaller
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires using flow charts to compare life-cycle stages of animals such as butterfly, frog, chicken, and human. The card describes nymphs in incomplete metamorphosis but does not use a flow chart or compare multiple life-cycle stages, so it does not directly support the required activity.

copy.en:
What does a nymph look like?

In incomplete metamorphosis, the nymph already looks like the adult insect, just smaller — it grows bit by bit.
copy.tl:
Ano ang hitsura ng nymph?

Sa di-ganap na metamorphosis, ang nymph ay kamukha na ng hingkod na insekto, mas maliit lang — unti-unti itong lumalaki.
copy.bis:
Unsay hitsura sa nymph?

Sa dili kompleto nga metamorphosis, ang nymph susama na sa hamtong nga insekto, mas gamay ra — hinay-hinay kining modako.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bright colors like red and yellow are used for safety because they bounce back light and catch our eyes easily!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that bright colors reflect light and are used for safety, but it does not describe sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed in a way that directly supports the competency's focus on exploring light sources and behavior. The reflection idea is only a passing mention, and the card is about color visibility, not light itself.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Bright colors like red and yellow are used for safety because they bounce back light and catch our eyes easily!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires guided investigations describing and illustrating reflection using plane/curved mirrors and refraction using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms. The card only mentions that bright colors bounce back light, with no reference to mirrors, lenses, prisms, or any investigation. It does not directly support the reflection/refraction content.

copy.en: Bright colors like red and yellow are used for safety because they bounce back light and catch our eyes easily! That's why construction vests and stop lights use them to stand out.
copy.tl: Ginagamit ang maliliwanag na kulay tulad ng pula at dilaw para sa kaligtasan dahil madali silang makita! Nagbabalik sila ng liwanag kaya agad napapansin ang mga construction vest at traffic light.
copy.bis: Gigamit ang hayag nga kolor sama sa pula ug dilaw para sa kaluwasan kay sayon makita! Mobalik sila og kahayag busa dali mamatikdan ang mga construction vest ug traffic light.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ocean food chains start with tiny plankton, eaten by small fish, which are then eaten by bigger fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw a simple food chain using living things from the Philippines and label them as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not draw a simple food chain of Philippine living things labeled as herbivores, carnivores, and omnivores.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ocean food chains start with tiny plankton, eaten by small fish, which are then eaten by bigger fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: A who-eats-who ocean chain is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Ocean food chains start with tiny plankton, eaten by small fish, which are then eaten by bigger fish
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the trophic levels of an organism as levels of energy in a food pyramid
assignedReviews.reason: A who-eats-who chain is not trophic levels as levels of energy in a food pyramid.

copy.en: Ocean food chains start with tiny plankton, eaten by small fish, which are then eaten by bigger fish.
copy.tl: Sa dagat, nagsisimula ang food chain sa maliliit na plankton na kinakain ng maliliit na isda, na kinakain naman ng mas malalaking isda.
copy.bis: Sa dagat, magsugod ang food chain sa gagmay nga plankton nga kaonon sa gagmay nga isda, nga kaonon usab sa dagkong isda.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ocean stores a huge amount of heat and releases it slowly, helping keep Earth's climate steady!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the ocean (a body of water) but does not identify local examples of landforms/bodies of water nor describe how they influence non-living and living components. It focuses on heat storage and climate steadiness, which is not the competency's instructional target.

copy.en: The ocean stores a huge amount of heat and releases it slowly, helping keep Earth's climate steady!
copy.tl: Ang karagatan ay nag-iimbak ng napakaraming init at dahan-dahan itong inilalabas, kaya nananatiling matatag ang klima ng Mundo!
copy.bis: Ang kadagatan naghupot og daghan kaayong kainit ug hinay-hinay kining gibuhian, mao nga nagpabilin nga lig-on ang klima sa Kalibutan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tides are the slow rising and falling of the whole sea caused by the moon.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun with the occurrence of tides
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that tides are caused by the moon. It does not relate the relative movements of the Earth, Moon, and Sun to tides, which is the core of the competency. The mention of the moon is a simplified cause, not an explanation of the relative motions.

copy.en: Tides aren't just big waves! Waves are made by wind and pass quickly. Tides are the slow rising and falling of the whole sea caused by the moon.
copy.tl: Hindi lang malalaking alon ang taog! Gawa ng hangin at mabilis ang alon. Ang taog ay dahan-dahang pagtaas at pagbaba ng buong dagat dahil sa buwan.
copy.bis: Dili lang dagkong balod ang taob! Gibuhat sa hangin ug paspas ang balod. Ang taob kay hinay nga pagsaka ug pagkanaog sa tibuok dagat tungod sa bulan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ocean has light zones: the sunlit zone (0-200m) has enough light for photosynthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes ocean depth zones, not local landforms or bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, or coastlines, and does not explain how such features influence living and non-living components. It shares the broad topic of bodies of water but does not support the competency's specific skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the sunlit zone (0-200m) has enough light for photosynthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that the sunlit zone has enough light for photosynthesis, but it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products. The mention of photosynthesis is incidental and does not teach the competency.

copy.en: The ocean has light zones: the sunlit zone (0-200m) has enough light for photosynthesis, the twilight zone (200-1000m) has very little light, and the midnight zone (1000m+) is totally dark.
copy.tl: Nahahati ang karagatan sa mga zone ayon sa liwanag: may sapat na liwanag ang euphotic zone (0-200m) para sa photosynthesis, kakaunti na lang ang liwanag sa twilight zone (200-1000m), at ganap na madilim ang midnight zone (1000m pataas).
copy.bis: Nabahin ang dagat sa mga zone base sa kahayag: adunay igo nga kahayag ang euphotic zone (0-200m) alang sa photosynthesis, gamay na lang ang kahayag sa twilight zone (200-1000m), ug hingpit nga ngitngit ang midnight zone (1000m pataas).

assignedReviews.card_evidence: She cleans them and fans fresh water over them the whole time, until they finally hatch.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify which groups of animals reproduce by giving birth to live young, such as mammals, and which reproduce by laying eggs, such as birds and reptiles
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a mother octopus caring for her eggs, but it does not identify which groups of animals reproduce by laying eggs versus giving birth, nor does it classify octopuses among egg-laying animals. It only mentions eggs incidentally without teaching the classification skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: She cleans them and fans fresh water over them the whole time, until they finally hatch.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows parental care of eggs, which is related to reproduction, but it does not describe the general characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce) or teach reproduction as a characteristic. It focuses on a specific behavior rather than the concept of reproduction.

copy.en:
How long does a mother octopus guard her eggs?

For many days or weeks! She cleans them and fans fresh water over them the whole time, until they finally hatch.
copy.tl:
Gaano katagal binabantayan ng inahing pugita ang itlog niya?

Sa loob ng maraming araw o linggo! Nililinis niya ito at hinihipan ng sariwang tubig hanggang sa mapisa ang mga itlog.
copy.bis:
Unsa kadugay bantayan sa inahan nga kugita ang iyang itlog?

Sulod sa daghang adlaw o semana! Ginahinlo niya kini ug ginahuypan og presko nga tubig hangtod mapusa ang mga itlog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Hans Christian Oersted discovered the amazing link between electricity and magnetism way back in 1820!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card names a famous foreign scientist and his discovery, but the competency specifically asks for identifying a scientist and their invention/s. Electromagnetism is a discovery/phenomenon, not an invention. The card does not support the skill of using secondary sources to identify inventions, so it is only related to the topic of famous scientists.

copy.en: Hans Christian Oersted discovered the amazing link between electricity and magnetism way back in 1820!
copy.tl: Natuklasan ni Hans Christian Oersted ang kahanga-hangang ugnayan ng kuryente at magnetismo noong 1820!
copy.bis: Nadiskobrehan ni Hans Christian Oersted ang katingad-an nga sumpay sa kuryente ug magnetismo niadtong 1820!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It gets its cool name from Georg Ohm.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to identify a famous Filipino and/or foreign scientist and their invention/s
assignedReviews.reason: The card names Georg Ohm as the source of the unit name but does not identify an invention by him. The ohm is a unit of electrical resistance, not an invention, so it does not directly support the competency's skill of identifying a scientist and their invention/s.

copy.en: The unit of electrical resistance is the ohm! It gets its cool name from Georg Ohm.
copy.tl: Ang yunit ng electrical resistance ay ang ohm! Nakuha niya ang pangalan nito kay Georg Ohm.
copy.bis: Ang yunit sa electrical resistance mao ang ohm! Nakuha niini ang ngalan gikan kang Georg Ohm.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it just forms a thicker layer on top!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes oil floating on water and being lighter than water, which touches on a non-uniform mixture but does not teach useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Adding more doesn't change that oil is lighter than water.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe that particles are constantly in motion, have spaces between them, attract each other, and move faster as the temperature increases (or with the addition of heat)
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses density/immiscibility of oil and water, not particle motion, spacing, attraction, or temperature effects on particles. It does not directly support the particle model competency.

copy.en: No matter how much oil you pour into water, it won't sink—it just forms a thicker layer on top! Adding more doesn't change that oil is lighter than water.
copy.tl: Kahit dumami ang langis na ibubuhos mo, hindi ito lulubog—lulutang lang nang mas makapal sa ibabaw! Ang pagdami ay hindi nagbabago na mas magaan ang langis kaysa tubig.
copy.bis: Bisan modaghan pa ang lana nga imong ibubo, dili gihapon kini molunod—maghimo lang og mas baga nga sapaw sa ibabaw! Ang pagdaghan dili mag-usab nga mas gaan kini kaysa tubig.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they are all lighter than water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses oil floating on water due to being lighter (density), not uniform or non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It does not directly support describing useful everyday examples of mixtures.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they are all lighter than water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume (solids: definite shape and volume; liquids: no definite shape, definite volume; gases: no definite shape or volume)
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oil as a liquid but does not describe properties of solids, liquids, and gases in terms of shape and volume. The content is about density/floatation, not the required state-property contrast.

copy.en:
Do all kitchen oils float on water?

Yes! Almost every kind like coconut oil, lard, or corn oil floats because they are all lighter than water!
copy.tl:
Lumulutang ba ang lahat ng kitchen oil sa tubig?

Oo! Halos lahat ng uri tulad ng langis ng niyog, mantika ng baboy, o langis ng mais ay lumulutang dahil mas magaan silang lahat kaysa tubig!
copy.bis:
Naglutaw ba ang tanang kitchen oil sa tubig?

Oo! Halos tanang matang sama sa lana sa lubi, tambok sa baboy, o lana sa mais naglutaw kay mas gaan silang tanan kaysa tubig!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It floats on the surface because it is lighter than seawater!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why oil floats on seawater due to being lighter, but it does not describe uniform or non-uniform mixtures, solutions, suspensions, or classify the oil-water combination as a mixture. It only touches on a phenomenon related to immiscible liquids.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It floats on the surface because it is lighter than seawater!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oil and seawater as substances but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It provides no instructional support for the definition of matter.

copy.en:
What happens when oil spills into the sea?

It floats on the surface because it is lighter than seawater!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari kapag may natapong oil sa dagat?

Lumulutang ito sa ibabaw dahil mas magaan ito kaysa seawater!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo kon may natapong oil sa dagat?

Molutaw kini sa ibabaw kay mas gaan kini kay sa seawater!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Oil and water do not mix because water molecules are polar while oil is nonpolar.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of immiscible liquids, which could be a non-uniform mixture, but it does not describe it as a mixture, nor does it contrast uniform vs non-uniform mixtures, solutions, or suspensions. The focus is on the particle-level reason for not mixing, not on classifying or describing mixture types.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They don't attract each other, so they stay separate instead of dissolving!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the role of the solute and solvent in a solution
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions dissolving and lack of attraction, but it does not identify a solute and solvent or explain their roles in a solution. Oil and water do not form a solution, so the card does not directly support identifying the role of solute and solvent.

copy.en: Oil and water do not mix because water molecules are polar while oil is nonpolar. They don't attract each other, so they stay separate instead of dissolving!
copy.tl: Hindi nahahalo ang langis at tubig dahil polar ang water molecules habang nonpolar ang langis. Hindi sila naghihilaan, kaya nananatili silang magkahiwalay sa halip na magtunaw!
copy.bis: Ang lana ug tubig dili magsagol kay polar ang water molecules samtang nonpolar ang lana. Dili sila magbiraay, mao nga magpabilin silang bulag imbis matunaw!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Okra's sliminess comes from mucilage, a soluble fiber
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses mucilage in okra and its digestive/cholesterol effects, not the outer parts of plants (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water and nutrient uptake. It shares the plant topic but does not support the competency's specific skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Okra's sliminess comes from mucilage, a soluble fiber
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant substance (mucilage) but does not describe the purpose of specialized structures like rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. Mucilage is not one of the listed structures, and the card does not address structure function.

copy.en: Okra's sliminess comes from mucilage, a soluble fiber that helps digestion and may lower cholesterol — Filipinos cook okra in many different ways.
copy.tl: Ang okra ay naglalaman ng mucilage—isang malagkit na soluble fiber—na nakakatulong sa digestive system at nagpapababa ng cholesterol; may iba't ibang paraan ang Pilipinas ng pagluluto nito.
copy.bis: Ang okra naglangkob og mucilage—usa ka malagkit nga soluble fiber—nga nakatabang sa digestive system ug mahimong makababa sa cholesterol; adunay lain-laing paagi ang Pilipinas sa pagluto niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The oldest living land animal is a tortoise named Jonathan, who is over 190 years old!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an example of a living thing (a tortoise) and its age, but does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It is only tangentially related to the competency.

copy.en:
Who is the oldest living land animal?

The oldest living land animal is a tortoise named Jonathan, who is over 190 years old!
copy.tl:
Sino ang pinakamatandang hayop sa lupa?

Ang pinakamatandang buhay na hayop sa lupa ay isang pagong na si Jonathan, na mahigit 190 taong gulang na!
copy.bis:
Kinsa ang pinakatigulang hayop sa yuta?

Ang pinakatigulang nga buhi nga hayop sa yuta usa ka baw nga ginganlag Jonathan, kapin na sa 190 anyos!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Methuselah, the world's oldest known tree, is more than 4,800 years old!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states the age of a tree. It does not describe growth, response, or reproduction, which are the characteristics named in the competency. Age is only tangentially related to growth.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Methuselah, the world's oldest known tree, is more than 4,800 years old!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: compare the life cycles of mammals from birth to adulthood, birds from egg to a mature organism, and plants from seed to a young plant, and then to a mature plant
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about an old tree and does not compare life cycles of mammals, birds, or plants from seed to mature plant. It provides no instructional support for the competency.

copy.en:
How old is the world's oldest tree?

Methuselah, the world's oldest known tree, is more than 4,800 years old!
copy.tl:
Ilang taon na ang pinakamatandang puno sa mundo?

Ang Methuselah, ang pinakamatandang puno sa mundo, ay mahigit 4,800 taong gulang na!
copy.bis:
Pila na katuig ang labing tigulang nga kahoy sa kalibutan?

Ang Methuselah, ang pinakatigulang nga kahoy sa kalibutan, kapin na sa 4,800 ka tuig ang panuigon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Do one written step, check it off, and stay focused.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the steps of a simple science investigation (What is the problem? What materials do you need? What do you need to do? What have you found out/learned?)
assignedReviews.reason: The card advises doing one written step at a time and checking it off, which is about following a procedure, not describing the steps of a simple science investigation (problem, materials, procedure, findings). It does not directly support the competency's content.

copy.en:
Why do one step at a time and check it off?

Skipping ahead makes groups lose their planned comparison! Do one written step, check it off, and stay focused.
copy.tl:
Bakit isang hakbang lang ang gagawin at tse-check?

Ang pagtalon sa susunod ay nakakapagpawala ng plano niyong paghahambing! Gawin ang isang hakbang, i-check, at mag-focus.
copy.bis:
Nganong usa ra ka lakang ang buhaton ug i-tsek?

Ang paglukso sa sunod makapawala sa inyong plano nga pagkumpara! Buhata ang usa ka lakang, i-check, ug mag-focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Onion and garlic belong to the same plant family, called Allium.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a single classification fact (onion and garlic are in the Allium family) but does not use a table to classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms). It does not directly support the competency's required activity or content.

copy.en:
What do onion and garlic have in common?

They're actually cousins! Onion and garlic belong to the same plant family, called Allium.
copy.tl:
Ano ang pagkakatulad ng sibuyas at bawang?

Magkamag-anak pala sila! Ang sibuyas at bawang ay parehong nasa iisang pamilya ng halaman na tinatawag na Allium.
copy.bis:
Unsay managsama sa sibuyas ug ahos?

Managsoon diay sila! Ang sibuyas ug ahos parehong sakop sa usa ka pamilya sa tanom nga gitawag og Allium.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: tiny phytoplankton and zooplankton near the surface, and glowing animals in the deep dark below
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card names living things and mentions light/dark, but it does not describe them as biotic and abiotic factors in an ecosystem, nor does it address water, temperature, or soil type as abiotic factors. It only uses ecosystem vocabulary without teaching the competency's concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The open ocean has layers full of different creatures
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a list or draw up a table with examples of animals and plants in a particular habitat, such as a garden, rice field, seashore, and mangrove swamp
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the open ocean as a habitat and gives a few organism examples, but it does not make a list or table of animals and plants in a particular habitat as required by the format-required competency. It is not a list/table and does not provide enough examples to support the skill.

copy.en: The open ocean has layers full of different creatures — tiny phytoplankton and zooplankton near the surface, and glowing animals in the deep dark below.
copy.tl: Ang bukas na karagatan ay may mga patong na puno ng iba't ibang nilalang — maliliit na phytoplankton at zooplankton sa ibabaw, at mga hayop na kumikinang sa napakalalim at madilim na bahagi.
copy.bis: Ang bukas nga dagat adunay mga patong nga puno sa lain-laing nilalang — gagmayng phytoplankton ug zooplankton sa ibabaw, ug mga mananap nga nagsidlak sa lawom ug ngitngit nga bahin.

Paano inihahanda ang ore bago kunin ang metal?

Ang malalaking piraso ng ore ay dinudurog at ginagawang pinong pulbos na parang buhangin! Mas madali nang mahiwalay ang metal mula sa basurang bato.

Giunsa pag-andam sa ore sa dili pa kuhaon ang metal?

How does your body remove waste?

Ang excretory system ang naghimo niini — naghimo og ihi ang bato, nagpawis ang panit, ug nagpagawas og carbon dioxide ang baga.
